proposal: The Mandate recommends that HUD restart the 2019 proposed rule that would prohibit noncitizens, including all mixed-status families, from living in federally assisted housing, and align with DHS public-charge reforms. It states that local welfare organizations, not the federal government, should house noncitizens.
remaining: The rule takes effect 2026-12-14; responsible entities must notify certain tenants within 30 days after the effective date, and current tenants' evidence is then collected on a staggered schedule (full compliance schedule not read).
Existing mixed-status households would be required to document eligible status or lose proration-based assistance as reexaminations occur; actual removals depend on implementation.

Whether a complete bar on mixed-status families, as the Mandate describes, is reached: the rule as read preserves assistance only to the extent a statute requires, and the treatment of the statutory 1995 preservation provision was not read.
Possible legal challenge: commenters raised Tenth Amendment, due process, Privacy Act and Violence Against Women Act objections, and none had been reported as filed by 2026-11-13.

status_summary: HUD published its final rule 'Housing and Community Development Act of 1980: Verification of Eligible Status' on 2026-11-12 (91 FR 72978, FR Doc. 2026-23003, RIN 2501-AE16), finalizing the proposal published 2026-02-20 (91 FR 8151); the rule takes effect 2026-12-14. It requires verification of status for every applicant and participant regardless of age, removes the option to decline to claim eligible status, and makes proration of assistance for mixed-status families a temporary condition pending verification where the statute permits, with an evidence-extension period of up to 60 days (30 days proposed). HUD's analysis in the rule estimates about 19,660 citizens or eligible noncitizens in affected programs have not yet provided proof of status and about 730 people previously declined to claim status. Because the rule is final but not yet effective, and the rule text read does not describe a complete bar on all mixed-status households, the record is in_progress; no lawsuit was found.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14218 (Ending Taxpayer Subsidization of Open Borders) is signed; HUD's 2026 proposal cites it as a basis.
HUD publishes a notice interpreting 'federal public benefit' under PRWORA to cover a range of HUD grant and housing programs, with immigration-verification guidance to follow.
The proposed rule 'Housing and Community Development Act of 1980: Verification of Eligible Status' is placed on public inspection at the Federal Register (8:45 a.m.), the day before publication.
Proposed rule published at 91 FR 8151: universal status verification, temporary-only proration, end of the 'do not contend' option; 60-day comment period.
Comment period closes (comments due 2026-04-21 per the Federal Register document and Stateline).

HUD publishes a 60-day notice (91 FR 37121) to extend approval of the existing information collection on the restriction on assistance to noncitizens and the consent form HUD-9886-A, citing section 214 of the Housing and Community Development Act of 1980; comments were due 2026-08-21, and the notice does not refer to the pending proposed rule.

DHS publishes a final rule on the public charge ground of inadmissibility (91 FR 45324, effective 2026-09-18) that rescinds the 2022 rule's public charge provisions and returns to case-by-case totality-of-the-circumstances assessment, in which receipt of means-tested public benefits may be considered; DHS's impact analysis discusses effects on mixed-status households. This is the DHS counterpart the Mandate asks HUD to align with, but it does not itself change HUD eligibility rules.

HUD issues a news release (HUD No. 26-091) on its final Verification of Eligible Status rule, saying the rule covers tenants already living in mixed-status households and requires documentation from people who claim U.S. citizenship or eligible immigration status.

HUD publishes the final rule 'Housing and Community Development Act of 1980: Verification of Eligible Status' (91 FR 72978, FR Doc. 2026-23003, RIN 2501-AE16, docket FR-6524-F-02), effective 2026-12-14: verification of status for all applicants and participants regardless of age, removal of the option to decline to claim eligible status, and proration of assistance for mixed families made a temporary condition pending verification where the statute permits; the evidence-extension period is up to 60 days (30 days proposed); 16,238 comments were received.

title: Bar noncitizens, including mixed-status families, from federally assisted housing
uncertainties: Stateline (2026-02-24) reports that HUD's Secretary wrote that about 24,000 people in HUD-assisted housing are likely ineligible and cites HUD's earlier analyses at about 25,000 mixed-status households; it also cites a figure of 80,000 people from the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities, which is not a HUD estimate. HUD's own estimates in the proposed rule's Federal Register text were not read (the regulatory impact sections fell beyond the portion read); the final rule's estimates are given in the status summary. A Federal Register API query for HUD documents on the proposed rule's title after 2026-04-01 returned none, and a query for HUD documents on noncitizens after 2026-04-22 returned only the 2026-06-22 information collection notice and a 2026-09-30 Privacy Act notice for a HUD data system (which lists citizenship fields and does not describe a new verification process). One general web search (2026-10-13) found only commentary and comment letters from the proposal period; no final rule, OMB review notice, lawsuit or congressional action was found, but a lawsuit would not necessarily appear in those results. The DHS public charge final rule was read only in its first part (the housing assistance section was cut off), so how it treats HUD programs was not verified. Whether a final rule that ends proration fits Section 214 is a legal question not resolved (inference from the statute as described in HUD's proposal). Update 2026-11-13: the final rule text was read on GovInfo (Federal Register PDF, first part only, through about page 72990 of a document of roughly 420,000 characters); the regulatory text of 24 CFR 5.520 and the treatment of the statutory preservation of assistance for families assisted as of 1995 were not read, and the Federal Register web page itself could not be opened on federalregister.gov in this review. The HUD news release (HUD No. 26-091) gives no effective date and cites nearly 200,000 tenants with incomplete or unknown verification from a HUD and DHS audit, which is not a count of households affected by this rule. Review 2026-11-13: the GovInfo PDF of the final rule was read again; its header (Vol. 91, No. 217, page 72978), the DATES section (effective 2026-12-14), RIN 2501-AE16, docket FR-6524-F-02, the 16,238 comments and the impact estimates match the record. The portion read states that preservation of assistance is made available only to the extent required by statute and mentions 1995-06-19 only as the date verification through SAVE began, so whether families assisted as of that date keep assistance remains unverified. The HUD news release was read on hud.gov.
